Essential 5-Language Travel Phrasebook

Quick Guide Practical Travel Language Tips

1. Lead with Polite Openers

Starting any question with Disculpe (Spanish), Sumimasen (Japanese), Māf kījiye (Hindi), or ʿAfwan / Law samaḥt (Arabic) immediately sets a warm, respectful tone before asking for directions or help.

2. Watch Speaker & Listener Gender

Spanish, Hindi, and Arabic adjust certain adjectives and verbs by gender — for example, perdido / perdida in Spanish or tāʾih / tāʾihah in Arabic ("lost"). Where two forms are shown, (m) is used by male speakers and (f) by female speakers.

3. Point to the Native Script

If pronunciation gets tricky in noisy stations or taxis, show the native Japanese, Devanagari (Hindi), or right-to-left Arabic script directly on your screen or printout — especially for addresses, dietary needs, and medical requests.

4. Modern Standard vs. Local Arabic

The Arabic phrases here use clear, polite Modern Standard Arabic understood across the Arab world, while everyday speech varies by region (e.g., ʿĀyiz mayyah in Egypt vs. Biddī mayy in the Levant for "I want water").
